Nonrefundable — it offsets tax on line 18 only.
_strings.@@6e922437c1f9: Treaty conformity — KS conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from KS income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the KS return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Kansas Form K-40 starts from federal adjusted gross income (2024 K-40 Line 1: "Federal adjusted gross income (as reported on your federal income tax return)"), and Kansas modifications are made only on Schedule S Part A. The 2024 Schedule S Part A "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" are an enumerated, closed list (lines A1-A7): A1 state/municipal bond interest, A2 KPERS contributions, A3 Kansas expensing recapture (K-120EX), A4 charitable contributions used for the Low Income Student Scholarship credit (K-70), A5 IRC 163(j) business interest expense carryforward, A6 unqualified First-Time Home Buyer savings account withdrawals, and A7 "other additions" (whose instructions list only federal income tax refunds, partnership/S-corp/fiduciary adjustments, community service contribution credit add-back, LQESP nonqualified withdrawals, energy-credit amortization, nonresident ad valorem taxes, and abortion-expense credits). There is NO add-back for federally tax-treaty-exempt income anywhere in Part A. Because income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and Kansas has no add-back, it flows through and is not re-taxed by Kansas -> conforms. (Source: 2024 Individual Income Tax Booklet, ip24.pdf, K-40 Line 1 and Schedule S Part A line-by-line instructions.)

_strings.@@c95603c12ce1: Credit for Taxes Paid to Other States — Kansas residents whose Kansas adjusted gross income (KAGI, line 3 of K-40) includes income earned in another state and who were required to pay income tax to that other state on that income. (Part-year residents filing as nonresidents may claim a version via a separate worksheet.) No credit for income from a state with no income tax. A copy of the other state's tax return must be enclosed (W-2s are not acceptable).
_strings.@@ccc346a9831e: Homestead Refund (property tax / circuit-breaker relief) — Kansas resident the entire year of 2024 who OWNED and occupied a Kansas home (homeowners only - the 2024 booklet states the program "is not available to renters"), AND meets one of: (1) born before January 1, 1969 (i.e., 55 or older); or (2) blind or totally and permanently disabled or a disabled veteran all of 2024; or (3) had a dependent child who lived with you the entire year, born before January 1, 2024 and under age 18 all of 2024. Related claims: K-40PT property tax relief (65+ with household income of $24,500 or less) and K-40SVR (65+ or disabled veteran or their surviving spouse, household income not more than $56,450); only ONE of K-40H/K-40PT/K-40SVR may be filed per household.

This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 STRUCTURAL CHANGE (SB 1, 2024 Special Session) — DO NOT USE 2023 FIGURES: Kansas replaced the 3.1%/5.25%/5.7% three-bracket schedule with TWO brackets — 5.2% on taxable income up to $23,000 ($46,000 married filing joint) and 5.58% above. Standard deductions rose to $3,605/$8,240/$6,180/$4,120 (single/MFJ/HoH/MFS). The exemption allowance was restructured from $2,250 per person to $18,320 (MFJ) / $9,160 (all other statuses) PLUS $2,320 per dependent, $2,320 additional for Head of Household, and $2,250 per disabled veteran. Base guidance: Supply K-40 Line 3, Kansas adjusted gross income (KAGI) = Line 1 federal AGI ('as reported on your federal income tax return') plus or minus Line 2 net modifications from Schedule S Part A (line A25). Most filers have no Kansas modifications, in which case Line 3 equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped standard deduction (K-40 Line 4) and the exemption allowance (Line 5) to reach Line 7 taxable income, to which the two-bracket schedule applies. EXEMPTION COUNT CONVENTION (2024): pass exemptions_count=1 for single/MFS filers and 2 for married filing jointly — the $9,160-per-count math reproduces the form's $9,160/$18,320 filing-status allowance exactly. Pass dependents_count = number of federal dependents (each $2,320; never count yourself or your spouse). HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD: pass exemptions_count=1 AND add 1 to dependents_count — the form grants HoH an additional $2,320 exemption ('If Filing Status above is Head of Household, enter $2,320'), which equals the per-dependent amount. Example: HoH with 1 dependent -> exemptions_count=1, dependents_count=2 (= $9,160 + $4,640). Missing it understates the exemption by $2,320. (For the FOOD SALES TAX CREDIT the HoH extra does NOT count — the booklet notes 'Head of Household is not allowed an additional exemption for food sales tax credit.') QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE maps to HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD in Kansas, not MFJ: the 2024 booklet Filing Status instruction says 'If your federal filing status is Qualifying Widow(er) with Dependent Child, check the Head of Household box.' Do not use a QSS->married_filing_jointly mapping for Kansas — compute QSS filers as head_of_household (single-status brackets, $6,180 standard deduction, $9,160 allowance + the extra $2,320 via dependents_count). Tax-table mandate below $100,000: K-40 Line 8 REQUIRES the Tax Tables when Line 7 taxable income is $100,000 or less; the Tax Computation Worksheet is used only above $100,000. The table uses $50-wide bands (computed at band midpoints), so bracket math may differ by a dollar or two within a table band — the filed form must use the table. NO zero-tax cliff for 2024 (change from 2023): the 2024 Kansas Tax Table starts at '$26 - $50 -> $2' and the Tax Computation Worksheet brackets start at $0 — the 2023 table's $0 rows up to $2,500/$5,000 and the cliff they created are GONE. Marginal bracket math applies from the first dollar. Rounded worksheet constants (re-derived for 2024): the Tax Computation Worksheet computes tax as 5.58% x the ENTIRE taxable income minus a subtraction amount. The exact continuity constants are $87.40 (Single/HoH/MFS: 5.58% x 23,000 - 5.2% x 23,000 = 1,283.40 - 1,196.00) and $174.80 (MFJ, at $46,000); the printed constants are $87 and $175. So above the breakpoint the filed worksheet result can be up to $0.40 HIGHER (Single/HoH/MFS) or $0.20 LOWER (MFJ) than exact marginal bracket math — up to $1 difference after whole-dollar rounding. One rate schedule covers Single, Head of Household, and Married Filing Separate ($23,000 breakpoint — the worksheet prints a single combined schedule for all three); it is duplicated per status here. Married Filing Joint has its own schedule with the breakpoint at exactly twice that ($46,000). Standard deduction for people 65 or older and/or blind is NOT modeled: the 2024 booklet worksheet replaces the base amounts with $4,455/$5,305 (Single, 1/2 boxes), $8,940/$9,640/$10,340/$11,040 (MFJ, 1-4 boxes), $4,820/$5,520/$6,220/$6,920 (MFS, 1-4 boxes), $7,030/$7,880 (HOH, 1/2 boxes) — i.e., +$850 per checked box for Single/HOH and +$700 per box for MFJ/MFS. Compute K-40 Line 4 from that worksheet in those cases. Kansas itemized deductions (Kansas Schedule A, K-40 Line 4) may be claimed instead of the standard deduction even if the federal return did not itemize — itemizers are not modeled; MFS spouses must both use the same method (if one itemizes, both must). Claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer: the 2024 instructions zero only the DEPENDENTS box ('enter "0" in the number of dependents box'); unlike 2023 they print no rule zeroing the filing-status allowance itself. Confirm the dependent-filer treatment at the DOR before relying on the $9,160 allowance for such a filer (see the pack's unverified list). CREDITS are not modeled by this op (they subtract from tax, not from income): the Food Sales Tax Credit is $125 per qualified exemption on K-40 Line 18 (nonrefundable, federal AGI $30,615 or less); the Kansas EITC is 17% of the federal EITC (Lines 17/23, refundable remainder); credit for child and dependent care expenses is 50% of the federal Form 2441 credit for 2024 (Line 14 — up from 25% in 2023); credit for taxes paid to other states (Line 13); NEW 2024 certificate credits (Workforce Retention K-93, Pregnancy Resource Act K-94) via Line 15. Kansas tax on lump sum distributions is not modeled: residents add 13% of the federal Form 4972 tax on K-40 Line 11. Nonresidents and part-year residents are not modeled: they compute the full-year tax on Line 8, then multiply by the Schedule S line B23 nonresident allocation percentage (K-40 Lines 9-10) to get nonresident tax. All K-40 money entries are whole dollars ('ENTER AMOUNTS IN WHOLE DOLLARS ONLY' printed on the 2024 form); the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches the form's presentation.
